grade9v3:question_repairs.clarify: Separate a bonded-atom direction from the number of shared pairs.
grade9v3:question_repairs.connect: The sigma component and pi component of a multiple bond connect the same atom pair.
grade9v3:question_repairs.way: Circle the distinct neighbours of carbon, then keep an independent bond-component inventory.
grade9v3:question_repairs.rule: HCHO carbon has three bonded-atom directions. C=O contributes one local domain, although its double bond contains one sigma and one pi component. Pi density is not confined to the internuclear axis.

grade9v3:question_repairs.pattern: HCN: two carbon directions, three C-N pairs. HCHO: three directions, two C-O pairs. Repeated multiplicity-as-direction counting suggests the misconception.

grade9v3:question_repairs.clarify: The counting centre is nitrogen, not every atom in NF3.

grade9v3:question_repairs.way: Circle nitrogen before counting; keep terminal-fluorine pairs in a separate inventory.
grade9v3:question_repairs.rule: NF3 has three nitrogen-to-fluorine directions and one nitrogen lone pair: four N-centred domains. Terminal F lone pairs do not add N-centred domains.
grade9v3:question_repairs.check: Changed check: substituting H for F leaves the local three-bond-plus-lone-pair N inventory unchanged in the introductory model.
grade9v3:question_repairs.probe: Count N-centred domains in NH3 and NF3. Then state where the F lone pairs are located.
grade9v3:question_repairs.pattern: Both N centres have four domains; F pairs are located at F. Repeated inclusion of terminal pairs identifies locality confusion.

microtopics.title: Steric electron-domain counting and multiple bonds
microtopics.badge_reason: Multiple bonds and terminal lone pairs frequently trigger incorrect steric number counts.
entry_assumptions: Recognises single and multiple bonds in simple Lewis structures.
microtopics.inferential_jump: An electron domain is a spatial direction of repulsive charge; all electrons between two bonded atoms constitute exactly one domain.

teaching_path.action: Count each bonded atom as one domain regardless of bond order.
teaching_path.why_valid: Multiple electron pairs between the same two nuclei share one internuclear direction.

teaching_path.action: Include only lone pairs residing directly on the central atom.
teaching_path.why_valid: Peripheral lone pairs on ligands do not influence the central atom's steric number.

teaching_path.action: Sum bonding domains and central lone pairs to obtain total electron domains.
teaching_path.why_valid: Total domains determine the underlying electrostatic geometry.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: Terminal-atom lone pairs add domains at the central atom.
misconceptions.diagnostic_prompt: Count N-centred domains in NH3 and NF3. Then state where the F lone pairs are located.
misconceptions.repair: NF3 has three nitrogen-to-fluorine directions and one nitrogen lone pair: four N-centred domains. Terminal F lone pairs do not add N-centred domains.

misconceptions.repair: Counting both C=O lines as separate domains confuses bond components with one bonded-atom direction. HCHO carbon has three domains.

exit_task.prompt: For hydrogen cyanide (H-C≡N), determine the number of electron domains around carbon and state whether the triple bond counts as one, two, or three domains.

answer.summary: Carbon has 2 electron domains (one C-H single bond and one C≡N triple bond). The triple bond counts as exactly one domain.
reasoning: Carbon has 2 attached atoms (H and N) and 0 lone pairs.
All 6 shared electrons in the triple bond occupy the single spatial direction between C and N.
answer.check: Steric number = 2 + 0 = 2 domains (linear geometry, sp hybridisation).

grade9v3:question_repairs.clarify: Distinguish the hybrid-set name from the number of orbitals in that set.
grade9v3:question_repairs.connect: A change of orbital basis preserves the number of independent orbitals.
grade9v3:question_repairs.way: Write one valence s plus n valence p orbitals; determine n and the resulting set size yourself.
grade9v3:question_repairs.rule: For second-period atoms, one 2s plus three 2p orbitals gives four sp3 hybrids. The superscript counts p inputs, not total outputs.
grade9v3:question_repairs.check: Changed check: an sp set has two hybrids because one s plus one p supplies two basis functions; use this conservation rule on the requested set.
grade9v3:question_repairs.probe: An sp2 set is proposed to contain two hybrids. How many input and output orbitals should it have? Then apply your method to an sp set.
grade9v3:question_repairs.pattern: Three for sp2, two for sp. Repeating the superscript-as-total rule in both cases suggests a held counting rule; correct changed cases after an isolated slip suggest an execution error.
grade9v3:question_repairs.transfer: Give the input/output inventory for sp without copying the original set.
grade9v3:question_repairs.wrong_idea: The superscript is the total number of hybrid orbitals.
grade9v3:question_repairs.label: Q1

grade9v3:question_repairs.clarify: The task asks for a local count before the introductory geometry label.
grade9v3:question_repairs.connect: Four bonding directions and no central lone pair use the demonstrated four-domain rule.
grade9v3:question_repairs.way: Inventory only carbon-centred domains; attach the known rule without reading shape from page angles.
grade9v3:question_repairs.rule: CH4 has four bonding domains, no carbon lone pair, and a tetrahedral introductory sp3 description. A Lewis layout encodes connectivity.
grade9v3:question_repairs.check: Changed check: CH3Cl still has four bonded neighbours around carbon even if the bonds have different properties.
grade9v3:question_repairs.probe: Count domains at C in CH3Cl and C in CH4. Does redrawing either as a cross change its count?
grade9v3:question_repairs.pattern: Both have four; changing drawing placement changes neither connectivity nor domain count. Repeated drawing-angle dependence suggests a spatial-model error.
grade9v3:question_repairs.transfer: Classify carbon in CH2Cl2 by domain inventory, not bond identity.
grade9v3:question_repairs.wrong_idea: The page layout is the molecular geometry.
grade9v3:question_repairs.label: Q3

grade9v3:question_repairs.clarify: Use the stated internuclear axis to classify the overlap.
grade9v3:question_repairs.connect: End-on and side-on are orientation/symmetry descriptions, not molecule-name clues.
grade9v3:question_repairs.way: Locate the axis and the density above/below it; name the two classes yourself.
grade9v3:question_repairs.rule: Sigma overlap is end-on/axial in the supplied sketch; pi overlap is lateral with a nodal plane containing the axis.
grade9v3:question_repairs.check: Changed check: rotating the entire sketch on the page leaves its classification unchanged relative to the rotated axis.
grade9v3:question_repairs.probe: Rotate the whole end-on sketch by 90 degrees on paper. Does it become pi? Compare that with rotating one p orbital relative to its neighbour.
grade9v3:question_repairs.pattern: Whole-picture rotation does not change sigma/pi classification; relative orbital rotation can change overlap. Conflating page orientation with relative geometry suggests the misconception.
grade9v3:question_repairs.transfer: Label a sigma component within a triple bond using its geometry.
grade9v3:question_repairs.wrong_idea: Turning a drawing on the page changes sigma into pi.
grade9v3:question_repairs.label: Q6

grade9v3:question_repairs.clarify: Map each set name to an orbital inventory, not its superscript alone.
grade9v3:question_repairs.connect: One s plus n p inputs gives n+1 hybrid outputs.
grade9v3:question_repairs.way: Write separate input/output ledgers for BF3 and CH4 before matching labels.
grade9v3:question_repairs.rule: BF3: three domains and three sp2 hybrids. CH4: four domains and four sp3 hybrids. For these centres use valence 2s/2p language rather than ambiguous 1s + 2p shorthand.
grade9v3:question_repairs.check: Changed check: sp uses two inputs and two hybrid outputs, providing a third case for the conservation rule.
grade9v3:question_repairs.probe: Compare proposed totals sp=1, sp2=2, sp3=3 against basis-function conservation. Give the corrected sequence.
grade9v3:question_repairs.pattern: The corrected sequence is 2,3,4. Repeating the shifted sequence suggests the superscript-as-total rule.

microtopics.title: Hybridisation, orbital conservation, and overlap symmetry
microtopics.badge_reason: Learners must correlate domain counts with conserved hybrid sets and classify overlap symmetry.
entry_assumptions: Understands basic s and p atomic orbital shapes.
microtopics.inferential_jump: The number of hybrid orbitals produced strictly equals the number of pure atomic orbitals mixed; end-on overlap gives cylindrical sigma symmetry, while lateral overlap produces a nodal plane.

teaching_path.action: Match the steric domain count to the required number of hybrid orbitals.
teaching_path.why_valid: Electrons repel into symmetric 3D directions requiring equivalent hybrid orbitals.

teaching_path.action: Combine one s orbital with the necessary p orbitals (sp, sp2, sp3) conserving total orbital count.
teaching_path.why_valid: Orbital conservation dictates that mixing n atomic orbitals yields n hybrid orbitals.

teaching_path.action: Classify bond overlaps: coaxial end-on as sigma (cylindrical) and lateral side-on as pi (nodal plane).

exit_task.prompt: BeCl2 has two bonding domains and zero central lone pairs. Identify the hybridisation of beryllium and state whether the Be-Cl bonds are sigma or pi.

answer.summary: Beryllium is sp hybridized (mixing 1s + 1p = 2 hybrid orbitals at 180°). Both Be-Cl single bonds are sigma bonds formed by coaxial end-on overlap.
reasoning: Steric number = 2 bonding domains + 0 lone pairs = 2 domains.
Two directions require sp hybridisation.
Single bonds formed along the internuclear axis are sigma bonds.
answer.check: Confirm that two hybrid orbitals yield linear geometry with cylindrical bond symmetry.

microtopics.title: 3D Stereochemical representation and qualitative models
microtopics.badge_reason: Translating flat 2D Lewis drawings into 3D wedge-dash geometry and understanding model boundaries are major sticking points.
microtopics.inferential_jump: Flat Lewis structures show connectivity, not 3D shape; wedge-dash conventions capture non-coplanar angles (109.5° / 107°), and VSEPR predicts geometry from domain repulsion without solving orbital wavefunctions.

teaching_path.action: Distinguish 2D topological connectivity (Lewis) from 3D spatial geometry (VSEPR/wedge-dash).
teaching_path.why_valid: Paper is flat, but four electron domains maximize separation in three dimensions.

teaching_path.action: Apply wedge-dash conventions: two bonds in-plane (lines), one forward (wedge), one backward (dash).
teaching_path.why_valid: Standard stereochemical notation makes non-coplanar depth explicit.

teaching_path.action: Delineate model boundaries: VSEPR predicts domain geometry and angles; it leaves orbital wavefunctions and spectra unresolved.
teaching_path.why_valid: Clear scope prevents over-claiming qualitative model abilities.

misconceptions.diagnostic_prompt: Draw NH3 and a tetrahedral four-bond NH4+ comparison. Mark which slot differs and recount the H atoms in each.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: A familiar chapter keyword selects the model.
misconceptions.diagnostic_prompt: Task A asks for atom/domain arrangement; task B asks which orbitals overlap along the bond axis. State what information each model must supply.
misconceptions.repair: VSEPR fits qualitative electron-domain arrangement. An orbital-overlap model addresses orbital participation. VSEPR does not itself calculate an exact experimental angle or full electronic structure.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: A Lewis cross proves a square-planar molecule.

exit_task.prompt: For water (H2O), sketch a 3D representation using wedge-dash notation showing both lone pairs. Explain why the H-O-H bond angle is ~104.5° rather than 90° or 180°.

answer.summary: Oxygen has 4 electron domains (2 bonding, 2 lone pairs) arranged tetrahedrally. Two bonds lie in-plane or with wedge/dash, while lone pairs occupy the other vertices. Lone pair repulsion compresses the ideal 109.5° tetrahedral angle to ~104.5°.
reasoning: Steric number = 2 bonding + 2 lone pairs = 4 domains.
Four domains repel into 3D tetrahedral geometry, not a 180° flat line or 90° square.
Lone-pair–lone-pair and lone-pair–bonding-pair repulsion compresses the H-O-H angle to 104.5°.
answer.check: Confirm 4 tetrahedral domains and trigonal planar/bent distinction.

relations.expression: Steric Number = (number of bonded atoms) + (number of lone pairs on central atom)
relations.meaning: Each bonded atom constitutes exactly one bonding domain regardless of bond order (single, double, triple); only lone pairs localized on the central atom contribute to its steric environment.

conditions: Count each attached atom as one domain regardless of single/double/triple bond order.

derivation.action: Count non-bonding valence electron pairs residing strictly on the central atom.
derivation.why_valid: Terminal lone pairs do not affect the central atom's steric number.

derivation.action: Sum bonded atoms and central lone pairs to determine total electron domains.

limits: Steric number assumes localized electron domains; delocalized resonance structures require evaluating resonance hybrids.

relations.expression: n atomic orbitals mixed -> n hybrid orbitals produced (sp -> 2, sp2 -> 3, sp3 -> 4)
relations.meaning: Linear combination of valence atomic orbitals conserves total orbital count; the number of directional hybrid orbitals formed equals the steric number of electron domains.
conditions: Hybridisation occurs between orbitals of comparable energy in the valence shell of the central atom.
Number of hybrid orbitals formed strictly equals the number of pure atomic orbitals hybridized.

derivation.action: Determine the required number of equivalent electron domain directions.

derivation.action: Check that the number of hybrid orbital directions matches the steric domain count.
derivation.why_valid: Matching avoids excess or missing orbital directions.

limits: Hybridisation is a valence-bond mathematical model, not a physical excitation step.
checks: Count pure atomic orbitals: 1s + 1p = 2 (sp); one valence s plus two valence p = 3 (sp2); one valence s plus three valence p = 4 (sp3).

relations.expression: σ bond: coaxial end-on overlap with cylindrical symmetry; π bond: lateral side-on overlap with nodal plane on internuclear axis
relations.meaning: Covalent bonds are classified by orbital overlap geometry: sigma bonds have electron density concentrated directly along the internuclear axis; pi bonds have electron density above and below that axis.
conditions: Internuclear axis is conventionally taken as the z-axis.
Atomic orbitals must have matching symmetry and favorable phase overlap.

items.title: Orbital overlap planes in allene (H2C=C=CH2)
items.prompt: In propadiene (allene, H2C=C=CH2), the central carbon atom forms two double bonds. Identify the hybridisation of the central carbon and deduce whether the two terminal CH2 groups lie in the same plane or in mutually perpendicular planes. Support your conclusion using orbital overlap symmetry.
items.source_label: Original competition-style transfer; not claimed as an official past-paper item.

answer.summary: The central carbon is sp hybridized, and the two terminal CH2 groups lie in mutually perpendicular planes.
reasoning: The central carbon has 2 bonding domains and 0 lone pairs, giving sp hybridisation with a linear 180° C-C-C backbone.
The central carbon has two unhybridized 2p orbitals (say, 2py and 2pz) that are mutually orthogonal (at 90° to each other).
One double bond is formed by lateral overlap with a 2py orbital of the left carbon, while the other double bond is formed by lateral overlap with a 2pz orbital of the right carbon.
Because the two pi bonds are oriented in perpendicular planes, the sigma frameworks and terminal CH2 groups must also be oriented in mutually perpendicular planes.

items.title: Nitrogen hybridisation in formamide and lone pair delocalisation
items.prompt: In an isolated amine (such as NH3), nitrogen is sp3 hybridized with a pyramidal geometry. In formamide (HCONH2), however, the nitrogen atom is experimentally observed to be nearly planar. Using electron domain and resonance arguments, explain why nitrogen's lone pair changes its effective steric behavior and hybridisation.
items.source_label: Original competition-style transfer; not claimed as an official past-paper item.

answer.summary: The nitrogen lone pair is delocalised into the adjacent C=O carbonyl pi system via resonance, requiring nitrogen to adopt sp2 hybridisation and planar geometry.
reasoning: The nitrogen lone pair participates in resonance: H2N-CH=O <-> H2N+=CH-O-.
For resonance overlap to occur, nitrogen's non-bonding pair must occupy an unhybridized 2p orbital parallel to the carbonyl pi bond.
This re-hybridizes nitrogen from sp3 to sp2, leaving three in-plane sigma bonding directions (trigonal planar, ~120°) and one perpendicular p orbital containing the delocalised pair.
